mock_data.title: Football Hooligans
mock_data.passage:
It is football time again. Currently, the qualifying rounds are being played to decide which countries will send teams to Japan and Korea for the 2002 World Cup. Soccer is becoming more and more popular on a worldwide scale and these qualifying legs are causing much excitement.

The game is popular at club level as well. Many fans go every week to support their team, whether the fixture is a home or away one, hoping to get a result. They all hope for an attacking game, with a lot of goals being scored. Obviously, they do not want to see a boring, defensive match where the players are aimlessly passing the ball to each other.

Sadly, not all the action always takes place on the pitch. All too frequently, there is action in the stands, too. Football supporters, most of whom declare their loyalty by sporting their team's colours, in the form of scarves or shirts, are not known for their quiet behaviour. They are often very noisy, shouting noisy encouragement to their team and singing rowdy, partisan songs.

There is much rivalry between supporters. Mostly, this is good-natured, but trouble can easily flare up. Fans get angry if they feel that a referee has made a wrong decision, perhaps giving one of their team a red or yellow card unfairly, or perhaps failing to notice a foul committed by a member of the other team when tackling.

When trouble breaks out in a football crowd, it can be difficult to control. Stadium officials often seat the opposing fans in separate parts of the ground as a precaution against fighting. However, preventing trouble is more difficult outside the ground. In the worst cases, riot police have to be called in.

Unfortunately, there are some fans who enjoy this violent aspect of football. These football hooligans really enjoy a running battle with the police, and incite other people to throw stones and bottles at them. They regard football not as a sport, but as an excuse for troublemaking. Inevitably, their behaviour spoils the reputation of the game.
mock_data.passageB1:
It's football season again! Many countries are playing games to see who will go to the World Cup. This time, it will be in Japan and Korea in 2002. Football, or soccer, is becoming more popular around the world. These games are very exciting.

Football is also popular at local clubs. Many fans go to games every week to support their team. They go to home games and away games. They hope their team will win. They want to see an exciting game with many goals. They don't want a boring game where players just pass the ball slowly.

Sadly, not everything happens on the field. Sometimes, there is trouble in the stands where the fans sit. Football fans usually wear their team's colors, like scarves or shirts, to show who they support. They are often very loud, cheering for their team and singing songs.

There is often a rivalry between different groups of supporters. Most of the time, it is friendly. But sometimes, trouble can start easily. Fans can get angry if they think the referee made a bad decision. For example, if a player gets a red or yellow card that the fans think is unfair. Or if the referee doesn't see a foul by the other team.

When trouble starts in a football crowd, it can be hard to control. Stadium staff often put fans from different teams in different parts of the stadium. This is to try and stop fights. But it is harder to stop trouble outside the stadium. Sometimes, the police have to come to stop riots.

Unfortunately, some fans enjoy the violence. These are called football hooligans. They like fighting with the police and making other people throw things. They don't see football as a sport. They just want to cause trouble. This spoils the game for everyone else. They incite others to join in the violence and cause damage. Their behavior can lead to arrests and stadium bans, but they often don't care. They just want to stir up trouble.
mock_data.passageB2:
As football fever grips the world once again, the qualifying rounds for major tournaments like the World Cup are in full swing. The sport's global appeal is undeniable, and these matches generate considerable excitement. At the club level, weekly games draw huge crowds, with fans flocking to stadiums, both home and away, hoping for a victory. The ideal match, in their eyes, is an attacking one, filled with goals and excitement. A dull, defensive game with endless, pointless passing is the last thing they want to see.

Unfortunately, the action isn't always confined to the pitch. All too often, unruly behaviour spills over into the stands. Football supporters, easily identifiable by their team's colours displayed on scarves and shirts, are known for their passionate, and sometimes boisterous, behaviour. They enthusiastically cheer on their team, singing loud, often partisan songs.

While rivalry between supporters is a natural part of the game, and mostly harmless, it can quickly escalate into something more serious. Fans can become enraged by perceived injustices, such as a referee's decision to issue an unfair card or overlook a foul committed by the opposing team. Such incidents can ignite tensions and lead to conflict.

When trouble erupts within a football crowd, it can be extremely difficult to control. Stadium authorities frequently segregate opposing fans in different sections of the ground as a preventative measure. However, managing potential conflict outside the stadium is even more challenging. In extreme cases, the police, sometimes in riot gear, are called in to restore order.

Sadly, a minority of fans actively seek out violence. These football hooligans see the game as an excuse for causing trouble, relishing clashes with the police and inciting others to throw objects. They view football not as a sport, but as an opportunity for mayhem. Their behaviour inevitably tarnishes the image of the game and undermines the enjoyment of genuine fans. Law enforcement agencies are constantly working to clamp down on such behaviour and ensure the safety of everyone attending football matches, striving to maintain the sport's positive reputation and safeguard the experience for all.
mock_data.passageC1:
As the preliminary stages unfold, determining which nations will vie for glory in the upcoming World Cup hosted by Japan and Korea, the global ascendancy of football continues apace. The sport’s appeal extends to the club level, where devoted fans flock to both home and away fixtures each week, their hopes pinned on a favourable outcome. The ideal scenario, of course, is an attacking, high-scoring game, a stark contrast to the drudgery of a defensive stalemate characterised by aimless passing.

Regrettably, the spectacle is not always confined to the pitch. All too often, disturbances erupt within the stands themselves. Football supporters, who typically profess their allegiance by donning their team's colours, are not generally known for their subdued demeanour. Indeed, they frequently engage in vociferous displays of support, chanting partisan songs with considerable gusto. While a healthy rivalry typically exists between sets of supporters, this can easily devolve into conflict. Frustration mounts when fans perceive unfair decisions from the referee, such as unwarranted disciplinary action against their own players or the overlooking of fouls committed by the opposition.

When unrest takes hold within a football crowd, maintaining order can prove exceedingly challenging. Stadium authorities often segregate opposing fans as a pre-emptive measure to mitigate the risk of clashes. However, preventing disturbances outside the stadium presents a far greater logistical hurdle. In the most extreme cases, the intervention of riot police becomes necessary, a grim indictment of the situation.

It is deeply regrettable that a subset of individuals derives pleasure from the violent aspects associated with football. These so-called football hooligans actively seek confrontations with law enforcement, inciting others to hurl projectiles. They perceive football not as a sporting contest, but rather as a pretext for engaging in disruptive behaviour. Inevitably, their actions tarnish the image of the sport, casting a shadow over the genuine passion and dedication of the vast majority of supporters and undermining the integrity of the game.

mock_data.translation:
Yana futbol vaqti keldi. Hozirgi kunda 2002-yilgi Jahon chempionati uchun Yaponiya va Koreyaga qaysi davlatlar jamoalarini yuborishini hal qilish uchun saralash bosqichlari (qualifying rounds) o'tkazilmoqda. Futbol (Soccer) butun dunyo miqyosida borgan sayin ommalashib bormoqda va bu saralash bosqichlari (legs) katta hayajon uyg'otmoqda.

O'yin klub (club) darajasida ham mashhur. Ko'plab muxlislar har hafta o'z jamoalarini qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun boradilar, uchrashuv (fixture) o'z maydonida (home) yoki safar o'yini (away) bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, natijaga erishishga (get a result) umid qiladilar. Ularning barchasi ko'plab gollar uriladigan hujumkor o'yinga umid qilishadi. Shubhasiz, ular o'yinchilar to'pni bir-birlariga maqsadsiz uzatadigan zerikarli, himoyaviy o'yinni ko'rishni xohlamaydilar.

Afsuski, barcha harakatlar har doim ham maydonda (pitch) sodir bo'lmaydi. Juda tez-tez tribunalarda (stands) ham harakatlar bo'lib turadi. Futbol ishqibozlari, ularning aksariyati o'z jamoalarining ranglarini (colours) sharflar yoki futbolkalar ko'rinishida kiyib, o'z sadoqatlarini bildirishadi, ular o'zlarining tinch xulq-atvori bilan tanilmagan. Ular ko'pincha juda shovqinli bo'lib, o'z jamoalariga shovqinli dalda berishadi va shovqinli, tarafkashlik (partisan) qo'shiqlarini kuylashadi.

Muxlislar o'rtasida katta raqobat mavjud. Ko'pincha bu yaxshi niyatda bo'ladi, lekin muammo osongina kelib chiqishi mumkin. Muxlislar hakam (referee) noto'g'ri qaror qabul qilganini, ehtimol ularning jamoasidan biriga adolatsiz ravishda qizil yoki sariq kartochka (yellow card) berganini yoki boshqa jamoa a'zosi to'pni olib qo'yishda (tackling) qilgan qo'polligini (foul) sezmaganini his qilsalar, g'azablanadilar.

Futbol muxlislari orasida to'polon ko'tarilganda, uni nazorat qilish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Stadion mulozimlari ko'pincha janjalga qarshi ehtiyot chorasi sifatida raqib muxlislarni maydonning (ground) alohida qismlariga joylashtiradilar. Biroq, maydon tashqarisida tartibsizliklarning oldini olish qiyinroq. Eng yomon holatlarda tartibsizliklarga qarshi politsiya (riot police) chaqirilishi kerak bo'ladi.

Afsuski, futbolning ushbu zo'ravonlik jihatidan zavqlanadigan ba'zi muxlislar ham bor. Ushbu futbol bezorilari (hooligans) politsiya bilan davomli to'qnashuvdan (running battle) juda zavqlanishadi va boshqa odamlarni ularga tosh va shishalar otishga undaydilar. Ular futbolni sport sifatida emas, balki to'polon qilish uchun bahona sifatida ko'radilar. Muqarrar ravishda ularning xulq-atvori o'yinning obro'siga putur yetkazadi.

mock_data.translationB1:
Mana yana futbol mavsumi! Ko'plab davlatlar Jahon chempionatiga kim borishini aniqlash uchun o'yinlar o'tkazmoqda. Bu safar u 2002-yilda Yaponiya va Koreyada bo'lib o'tadi. Futbol, ​​yoki soccer, butun dunyo bo'ylab tobora ommabop bo'lib bormoqda. Bu o'yinlar juda hayajonli.

Futbol mahalliy klublarda ham mashhur. Ko'plab muhlislar har hafta o'z jamoasini qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun o'yinlarga borishadi. Ular uy o'yinlariga va safar o'yinlariga borishadi. Ular o'z jamoasi g'alaba qozonishiga umid qilishadi. Ular ko'plab gollar urilgan hayajonli o'yinni ko'rishni xohlashadi. Ular o'yinchilar shunchaki to'pni sekin uzatadigan zerikarli o'yinni xohlashmaydi.

Afsuski, hamma narsa maydonda sodir bo'lmaydi. Ba'zan, tribunada, muxlislar o'tiradigan joyda muammo bo'ladi. Futbol muxlislari odatda o'z jamoasini kim qo'llab-quvvatlashini ko'rsatish uchun sharflar yoki futbolkalar kabi jamoa ranglarini kiyishadi. Ular ko'pincha juda baland ovozda bo'lishadi, o'z jamoasini qo'llab-quvvatlashadi va qo'shiqlar kuylashadi.

Ko'pincha turli guruh tarafdorlari o'rtasida raqobat mavjud. Ko'p hollarda, u do'stona. Ammo ba'zan, muammo osonlik bilan boshlanishi mumkin. Agar ular hakam yomon qaror qabul qildi deb hisoblasalar, muxlislar g'azablanishi mumkin. Masalan, agar o'yinchi muxlislar adolatsiz deb hisoblagan qizil yoki sariq kartochka olsa. Yoki agar hakam boshqa jamoaning qoidabuzarligini ko'rmasa.

Futbol olomonida muammo boshlanganda, uni nazorat qilish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Stadion xodimlari ko'pincha turli jamoalardan kelgan muxlislarni stadionning turli qismlariga joylashtiradilar. Bu janjallarni to'xtatishga harakat qilish uchun. Ammo stadion tashqarisida muammoni to'xtatish qiyinroq. Ba'zan, politsiya tartibsizliklarni to'xtatish uchun kelishi kerak.

Afsuski, ba'zi muxlislar zo'ravonlikdan rohatlanishadi. Bular futbol bezorilaridir. Ular politsiya bilan urushishni va boshqa odamlarni narsalar uloqtirishga majbur qilishni yaxshi ko'radilar. Ular futbolni sport deb hisoblashmaydi. Ular shunchaki muammo tug'dirmoqchi. Bu hamma uchun o'yinni buzadi. Ular boshqalarni zo'ravonlikka qo'shilishga undanmoqda va zarar yetkazmoqda. Ularning xulq-atvori hibsga olishlarga va stadiondan chetlatishlarga olib kelishi mumkin, ammo ular ko'pincha ahamiyat bermaydilar. Ular shunchaki muammo qo'zg'atmoqchi.
mock_data.translationB2:
Futbol isitmasi yana butun dunyoni qamrab olayotgan bir paytda, Jahon chempionati kabi yirik turnirlarning saralash bosqichlari qizg'in davom etmoqda. Bu sport turining global mashhurligi shubhasiz va bu o'yinlar katta hayajon uyg'otadi. Klublar darajasida har haftalik o'yinlar ulkan olomonni jalb qiladi, muxlislar g'alaba umidida o'z jamoalarini qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun uyda ham, safarda ham stadionlarga oqin bo'lishadi. Ularning nazarida ideal o'yin - bu gollar va hayajonga to'la hujumkor o'yin. Ular zerikarli, himoyaviy o'yinni cheksiz, ma'nosiz uzatmalar bilan ko'rishni xohlashmaydi.

Afsuski, har doim ham harakat maydon bilan cheklanmaydi. Ko'pincha bezori xatti-harakatlar tribunaga ham o'tadi. Futbol muxlislari, sharf va ko'ylaklarda o'z jamoalarining ranglarini namoyish etish orqali osonlik bilan tanib olinadi, ular o'zlarining ehtirosli va ba'zan shovqinli xulq-atvorlari bilan mashhur. Ular o'z jamoalarini qizg'in qo'llab-quvvatlab, baland, ko'pincha tarafkash qo'shiqlarni kuylashadi.

Muxlislar o'rtasidagi raqobat o'yinning tabiiy qismi bo'lsa-da va asosan zararsiz bo'lsa-da, u tezda jiddiyroq narsaga aylanib ketishi mumkin. Muxlislar hakamning adolatsiz kartochka berish qarori yoki raqib jamoa tomonidan qilingan qo'pollikni e'tibordan chetda qoldirish kabi adolatsizliklar tufayli g'azablanishi mumkin. Bunday hodisalar keskinlikni olovlantirib, mojarolarga olib kelishi mumkin.

Futbol olomonida muammo boshlanganda, uni nazorat qilish juda qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Stadion ma'murlari oldini olish choralari sifatida ko'pincha raqib muxlislarni stadionning turli qismlariga ajratishadi. Biroq, stadion tashqarisida yuzaga kelishi mumkin bo'lgan mojarolarni boshqarish yanada qiyinroq. Favqulodda hollarda, tartibni tiklash uchun politsiya, ba'zan tartibsizliklarga qarshi jihozlangan holda chaqiriladi.

Afsuski, muxlislarning ozchiligi zo'ravonlikni faol ravishda izlaydi. Bu futbol bezorilari o'yinni muammo keltirish uchun bahona sifatida ko'rishadi, politsiya bilan to'qnashuvlardan zavqlanishadi va boshqalarni narsalar uloqtirishga undashadi. Ular futbolga sport sifatida emas, balki tartibsizliklar uchun imkoniyat sifatida qarashadi. Ularning xatti-harakatlari muqarrar ravishda o'yinning obro'sini dog' qiladi va haqiqiy muxlislarning zavqini yo'qqa chiqaradi. Huquqni muhofaza qilish organlari bunday xatti-harakatlarga qarshi qattiq kurashish va futbol o'yinlariga tashrif buyurgan har bir kishining xavfsizligini ta'minlash, sportning ijobiy obro'sini saqlash va barcha uchun tajribani himoya qilish uchun doimiy ravishda ishlamoqda.

Yaponiyada va Koreyada bo'lib o'tadigan kelgusi Jahon chempionatida qaysi davlatlar g'alaba uchun kurashishi aniqlanadigan dastlabki bosqichlar boshlanishi bilan futbolning global yuksalishi jadallik bilan davom etmoqda. Sportning jozibadorligi klub darajasiga ham taalluqli bo'lib, u yerda sodiq muxlislar har hafta uy va safar o'yinlariga oqin kelishadi, ularning umidlari ijobiy natijaga bog'langan. Albatta, eng ideal ssenariy - bu hujumkor, yuqori ballli o'yin, bu maqsadga yo'naltirilmagan uzatmalardan iborat himoyaviy zerikish bilan keskin farq qiladi.

Afsuski, tomosha har doim ham maydon bilan chegaralanmaydi. Ko'pincha, tartibsizliklar tribunalarning ichida sodir bo'ladi. Odatda jamoasining ranglarini kiyib, o'z sadoqatini e'lon qiladigan futbol muxlislari, odatda, bosilgan xulqi bilan tanilgan emas. Haqiqatan ham, ular tez-tez shovqinli qo'llab-quvvatlash namoyishlarida qatnashadilar, katta ishtiyoq bilan partizan qo'shiqlarini kuylashadi. Muxlislar o'rtasida odatda sog'lom raqobat mavjud bo'lsa-da, bu osongina nizolarga aylanib ketishi mumkin. Muxlislar hakamdan adolatsiz qarorlarni sezganlarida, masalan, o'z o'yinchilariga nisbatan asossiz intizomiy choralar ko'rilganda yoki raqib tomonidan qilingan qoidabuzarliklarga e'tibor berilmaganda, norozilik kuchayadi.

Futbol olomonida tartibsizliklar boshlanganida, tartibni saqlash juda qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Stadion ma'murlari to'qnashuvlar xavfini kamaytirish uchun oldindan ko'rilgan chora sifatida raqib muxlislarni ko'pincha ajratib qo'yishadi. Biroq, stadion tashqarisida tartibsizliklarning oldini olish ancha katta logistik to'siqni keltirib chiqaradi. Eng og'ir holatlarda, tartibsizliklarga qarshi politsiyaning aralashuvi zarur bo'lib qoladi, bu vaziyatning qabih ayblovi hisoblanadi.

Futbol bilan bog'liq zo'ravonlik jihatlaridan ba'zi odamlar zavq olishlari juda achinarli. Bu o'zini futbol xuliganlari deb ataydiganlar huquqni muhofaza qilish organlari bilan to'qnashuvlarni faol ravishda izlaydilar, boshqalarni narsalarni otishga undaydilar. Ular futbolni sport musobaqasi emas, balki buzuvchi xatti-harakatlar qilish uchun bahona sifatida qabul qiladilar. Shubhasiz, ularning harakatlari sportning obro'sini bulg'aydi, muxlislarning katta qismining chinakam ishtiyoqi va fidoyiligiga soya soladi va o'yinning halolligini buzadi.
